newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINES SAID A GOOD BUY DESPITE PESO FALL.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINES SAID A GOOD BUY DESPITE PESO FALL.

text.p: The Philippines remained a good buy despite the sharp peso depreciation which had left its financial markets badly shaken, reports by two international investment houses said.
"We continue to believe that the fundamentals in the Philippines remain solid," Merrill Lynch's August report, made available to Reuters on Tuesday, said.
The report said a tight monetary policy was expected to be maintained to rein in inflation and restore market confidence.
Merrill said it was recommending buying Philippine Treasury bills, especially the long-termed ones as they were likely to yield between 10 and 18 percent.
Treasury bills have been on the rise after the central bank raised its benchmark rates to defend the peso from persistent speculative attacks.
Despite the de facto devaluation on July 11, the central bank has still kept its rates relatively high.

"After losing some 10 percent of its value following the July 11 devaluation, we believe that the Philippine peso is likely to remain stable for the rest of the year and the Philippine peso is the only Southeast Asian currency that we currently recommend holding," the report said.
It said Philippine Brady and euro bonds would provide good investments since their valuations had become attractive.
Bankers Trust analyst Cristina Infante predicted the Hong Kong and Manila equities markets would be the best performing markets in the region.

"The economy remains robust - strong exports and domestic demand should provide strong support in corporate earnings in the second half - and we maintain our overweight recommendation on the Philippine market," Infante said in her report for August.
The stock composite index has fallen more than 20 percent since April 1 when the speculative attack on the peso started. It closed at 2,535.40 on Tuesday.
Infante said property and banking stocks provided the best investment opportunities.
